title: Art Collective Circle
description: Four artists sharing a studio space in Brooklyn connected through neighboring studios, joint exhibitions, a shared mentor, and material sharing. Rich in artistic details, exhibition history, and creative processes.

people.name: Maren Solberg
people.profile: Norwegian-American painter known for large-scale urban murals. Grew up in Minneapolis. Studio neighbor with Jun, shares exhibition space with Zara.

observations.text: Maren Solberg grew up in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and her parents emigrated from Bergen, Norway in 1988.
Maren Solberg rents Studio 4A at the Gowanus Arts Building on 3rd Avenue in Brooklyn.
Maren Solberg and Jun Takeda have adjacent studios at the Gowanus Arts Building and share a wall-mounted tool rack between their spaces.
Maren Solberg and Zara Osei co-curated an exhibition called 'Thresholds' at the BRIC Arts Media gallery in Fort Greene in April 2024.
Maren Solberg earned her MFA in painting from the Rhode Island School of Design in 2018.
Maren Solberg completed a 40-foot mural of the Brooklyn waterfront on the side of a warehouse on Van Brunt Street in Red Hook in March 2024.
Maren Solberg studied under Professor Claudia Venn at RISD, who also mentored Zara Osei during a summer workshop.
Maren Solberg's primary medium is oil paint, and she buys her Williamsburg brand paints in bulk from New York Central Art Supply.
Maren Solberg's father, Erik Solberg, is a carpenter who builds custom furniture in Minneapolis.
Maren Solberg was awarded a $15,000 grant from the Joan Mitchell Foundation in January 2024.
Maren Solberg sold a large-scale oil painting titled 'Fjord Memory' to a private collector for $8,500 in June 2024.
Maren Solberg speaks English and Norwegian fluently.
Maren Solberg lives in a third-floor walkup apartment on Dean Street in Boerum Hill with her partner, Kai.
Maren Solberg teaches a weekend oil painting workshop at the Brooklyn Art Center on Atlantic Avenue.
Maren Solberg traveled to Oslo for two weeks in July 2023 to study Edvard Munch's techniques at the Munch Museum.
Maren Solberg rides a turquoise Bianchi road bike to her studio every day.
Maren Solberg's favorite museum in New York is the Dia Beacon for its large-scale installations.
Maren Solberg lends her oil painting supplies to Ines Varga, who uses oil-based glazes on her ceramic pieces.
Maren Solberg's favorite restaurant in Brooklyn is Sahadi's on Atlantic Avenue for their hummus plate.
Maren Solberg is preparing a solo show of 12 new paintings for the Minus Space gallery in Dumbo, opening in October 2024.

people.name: Jun Takeda
people.profile: Japanese-American sculptor working with reclaimed metal. Grew up in Portland, Oregon. Studio neighbor with Maren, shares exhibition space with Ines.

observations.text: Jun Takeda grew up in Portland, Oregon, and moved to New York in 2019 after graduating from the Pacific Northwest College of Art.
Jun Takeda rents Studio 4B at the Gowanus Arts Building on 3rd Avenue in Brooklyn, directly next to Maren Solberg.
Jun Takeda and Maren Solberg have adjacent studios and share a wall-mounted tool rack between their spaces.
Jun Takeda and Ines Varga exhibited together in a two-person show called 'Fire and Form' at the Greenpoint Gallery in February 2024.
Jun Takeda welds sculptures from reclaimed industrial metal, primarily sourced from the Gowanus scrapyards.
Jun Takeda's father, Hiroshi Takeda, is an architect at ZGF Architects in Portland.
Jun Takeda speaks English and Japanese fluently.
Jun Takeda was selected for the Socrates Sculpture Park emerging artist fellowship and installed a 12-foot welded steel piece there in May 2024.
Jun Takeda lives in a loft apartment in Bushwick on Knickerbocker Avenue that doubles as overflow workspace.
Jun Takeda completed a commissioned sculpture for the lobby of a tech company called Meridian Labs in the Flatiron District for $12,000 in August 2024.
Jun Takeda practices kendo at the Brooklyn Kendo Club on Flatbush Avenue every Wednesday and Saturday evening.
Jun Takeda built a custom welding table for Ines Varga's kiln room as a birthday gift in March 2024.
Jun Takeda's favorite sculptor is Richard Serra.
Jun Takeda earned his BFA in sculpture from the Pacific Northwest College of Art in 2019.
Jun Takeda teaches an introductory welding workshop at the Gowanus Arts Building on the first Saturday of each month.
Jun Takeda drives a white 2017 Ford Transit cargo van he uses to transport sculptures to exhibitions.
Jun Takeda traveled to Naoshima Island in Japan in December 2023 to visit the Chichu Art Museum and Benesse House.
Jun Takeda won a $5,000 emerging artist prize from the Brooklyn Arts Council in September 2023.
Jun Takeda's favorite restaurant in Brooklyn is Okonomi on Metropolitan Avenue for their traditional Japanese breakfast.
Jun Takeda is building a series of kinetic wind sculptures made from salvaged copper pipe for a group show at Pioneer Works in Red Hook.

people.name: Zara Osei
people.profile: Ghanaian-American photographer documenting immigrant communities. Grew up in the Bronx. Shares a mentor lineage with Maren, exhibition partner with Maren.

observations.text: Zara Osei grew up in the Morrisania neighborhood of the Bronx, and her parents immigrated from Accra, Ghana in 1990.
Zara Osei rents Studio 4C at the Gowanus Arts Building on 3rd Avenue in Brooklyn.
Zara Osei and Maren Solberg co-curated an exhibition called 'Thresholds' at the BRIC Arts Media gallery in Fort Greene in April 2024.
Zara Osei and Ines Varga share a darkroom and print station on the 3rd floor of the Gowanus Arts Building.
Zara Osei earned her MFA in photography from the International Center of Photography in 2020.
Zara Osei studied under Professor Claudia Venn during a summer intensive at RISD in 2017, the same mentor who taught Maren Solberg.
Zara Osei shoots primarily on a Mamiya 7 II medium format film camera.
Zara Osei published a photo essay on Ghanaian immigrant families in Flatbush in The New Yorker's photo issue in June 2024.
Zara Osei speaks English, Twi, and French fluently.
Zara Osei's ongoing project 'Diaspora Kitchen' documents the cooking traditions of 40 immigrant families across all five boroughs of New York.
Zara Osei lives in a rent-stabilized apartment in Crown Heights on Nostrand Avenue.
Zara Osei won the W. Eugene Smith Memorial Fund Grant of $40,000 in October 2023 for her 'Diaspora Kitchen' project.
Zara Osei's mother, Abena Osei, is a registered nurse at Montefiore Medical Center in the Bronx.
Zara Osei teaches a documentary photography course at the Bronx Documentary Center on 151st Street on Thursday evenings.
Zara Osei traveled to Accra, Ghana for three weeks in January 2024 to photograph her extended family for the 'Diaspora Kitchen' series.
Zara Osei's favorite photographer is Gordon Parks.
Zara Osei takes the G train from Crown Heights to the Gowanus studio, a 20-minute commute.
Zara Osei organized a community photo walk through Prospect Park in May 2024 that attracted 35 participants.
Zara Osei's favorite restaurant in Brooklyn is Peppa's Jerk Chicken on Flatbush Avenue.
Zara Osei was invited to exhibit 20 prints from 'Diaspora Kitchen' at the Aperture Foundation gallery in Chelsea, opening in November 2024.

people.name: Ines Varga
people.profile: Hungarian-American ceramicist experimenting with architectural-scale clay work and custom glazes. Grew up in Cleveland. Shares darkroom with Zara, exhibited with Jun.

observations.text: Ines Varga grew up in Cleveland, Ohio, in the Tremont neighborhood, and her parents emigrated from Budapest, Hungary in 1993.
Ines Varga rents Studio 4D at the Gowanus Arts Building on 3rd Avenue in Brooklyn.
Ines Varga and Jun Takeda exhibited together in a two-person show called 'Fire and Form' at the Greenpoint Gallery in February 2024.
Ines Varga and Zara Osei share a darkroom and print station on the 3rd floor of the Gowanus Arts Building.
Ines Varga earned her BFA in ceramics from the Cleveland Institute of Art in 2019 and an MFA from Alfred University in 2022.
Ines Varga formulates her own ceramic glazes and developed a signature copper-red reduction glaze she calls 'Paprika'.
Ines Varga uses oil-based glazes that she purchases from Maren Solberg, who buys them in bulk.
Ines Varga fired a 4-foot ceramic column in a wood-fired anagama kiln at the Watershed Center for the Ceramic Arts in Maine in September 2023.
Ines Varga speaks English and Hungarian fluently.
Ines Varga was selected for the Ceramic Arts Residency at the Archie Bray Foundation in Helena, Montana for summer 2025.
Ines Varga lives in a converted warehouse apartment in Gowanus, a five-minute walk from the studio building.
Ines Varga sells functional pottery — mugs, bowls, and plates — at the Brooklyn Flea Market in Dumbo on weekends, averaging $800 in sales per Saturday.
Ines Varga's mother, Katalin Varga, teaches Hungarian language and literature at Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland.
Ines Varga received a custom welding table for her kiln room from Jun Takeda as a birthday gift in March 2024.
Ines Varga's favorite ceramic artist is Peter Voulkos.
Ines Varga teaches a hand-building ceramics class on Tuesday evenings at the 92nd Street Y in Manhattan.
Ines Varga won a $3,000 craft innovation award from the American Craft Council in November 2023 for her 'Paprika' glaze formula.
Ines Varga traveled to Shigaraki, Japan in August 2023 to study traditional wood-fired kiln techniques at the Shigaraki Ceramic Cultural Park.
Ines Varga's favorite restaurant in Brooklyn is Frankel's Delicatessen on Greenpoint Avenue for their pastrami sandwich.
Ines Varga is building a custom outdoor wood-fired kiln on the rooftop of the Gowanus Arts Building, expected to be completed by December 2024.
